text: Hi, just getting started this week. I've been reading the LoRA paper and the follow-up work on rank selection. My plan is to sweep rank r in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64} on LLaVA-1.5-7B using the LLaVA-Instruct-150k dataset. Should take 3-4 days to get initial results. Quick question: should I fix alpha = 2r (as in the original paper) or also sweep alpha independently?
Also, should I be evaluating on SEED-Bench or MMBench first? I have compute for one full sweep before the weekend.
Started rank=4 baseline. Training loss at step 100: 1.34. Seems reasonable. I'll check in tomorrow with step 500 results.
Step 500 results for rank=4: val loss 0.94, SEED-Bench score 63.2. Starting rank=8 now. The training is stable, no OOM issues on the A100.
Small update: rank=8, step 200, val loss already below rank=4 final (0.89 vs 0.94). Looking promising. Will finish rank=8 overnight.
Rank=8 done: SEED-Bench 64.7 (+1.5 vs rank=4). Memory usage: 18.3GB peak. Starting rank=16 tomorrow.
Rank=16 result: SEED-Bench 65.1. Only +0.4 over rank=8 but memory jumped to 21.7GB. Diminishing returns starting to show. Running rank=32 now.
Rank=32 crashed — OOM at step 47. 24GB VRAM limit hit. I'm going to try gradient checkpointing. Does that usually work well with LoRA, or does it interfere with the adapter gradients?
Gradient checkpointing worked! Rank=32 now running, ~19.1GB with checkpointing. Will have results tomorrow.

Rank=32 complete: SEED-Bench 65.3. Essentially same as rank=16 (65.1). Training took 2.1x longer due to checkpointing. My working hypothesis: sweet spot is rank=8 or rank=16 for this task. Starting rank=64 with checkpointing today.

Rank=64 result: SEED-Bench 65.2, lower than rank=32 (65.3)! Overparameterized? Or just noise? Ran it twice and got 65.1 and 65.2. I think rank=8 or 16 is genuinely optimal here. Should I do statistical testing or is this margin too small to matter?

Starting to write up the rank sweep results. One thing I noticed: the validation loss curves for rank>=16 are very similar, but the SEED-Bench scores diverge slightly. Does this suggest SEED-Bench has high variance, or that val loss is not predictive of downstream benchmark perf?
Also planning to test QLoRA (4-bit quantization + LoRA) to see if I can get rank=32 performance within the rank=8 memory budget. Any concerns with QLoRA stability for VLMs specifically?

QLoRA rank=32 result: SEED-Bench 64.9, using only 14.2GB. Slightly below full-precision rank=32 (65.3) but much more memory-efficient. I think QLoRA rank=32 is the Pareto-optimal configuration for production use. Does this seem like a publishable finding or is it well-known already?

One more experiment: tested rank=8 with alpha=8 vs alpha=16 vs alpha=32. Results: SEED-Bench 64.5 / 64.7 / 64.6. So alpha has minimal effect at fixed rank, consistent with prior work. I think I have enough for a clean ablation table now.

Drafted the experimental section. I have rank sweep, alpha ablation, and QLoRA results. Should I also test cross-task transfer — i.e., does a rank=8 LoRA trained on LLaVA-Instruct generalize to a different VQA dataset, or does it overfit to the fine-tuning distribution?

Cross-task: tested on GQA (zero-shot from LLaVA-Instruct LoRA). Rank=8: 58.3, Rank=16: 58.7, Rank=32: 58.4. All close. Generalization seems comparable across ranks, which is actually reassuring. The rank choice doesn't seem to affect generalization.
